html:
SMTO-CAP-0007 — That program name can't be used in a Shell rule

GUID: 8c771287-2e7a-455f-8dcc-8b085ce56eb4
Slug: capability-executable-invalid
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • A Shell executable rule must name just one program, like curl, or its exact path. This entry had spaces, options or symbols in it, so SMTO didn't save the rule.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Capabilities by the message box, or Settings › Setup › Capabilities, and find Shell executable rules. This is where SMTO keeps the programs that Shell commands should prefer or avoid.
  2. In the box, type only the program name, such as curl, or its full path, such as /usr/bin/curl. Leave out spaces, options like -s, and symbols like | or $. SMTO matches the program itself, and extra command text makes it unclear which program the rule is for.
  3. Select + Prefer or − Exclude, then select Apply. The rule is only checked and saved when you apply your changes.

What success looks like

  • The program appears under Shell executable rules and the Capabilities window closes without an error.

If it still fails

  • If you didn't type this entry yourself, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO so they can fix it where it came from. Don't keep submitting the same entry; it will be rejected each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Capability policy validation (executable_basename) rejected a preferred_shell_executables or excluded_shell_executables entry that is not a plain name or slash-separated path of [A-Za-z0-9_.+@-], or whose basename is '.', '..' or starts with '-'.

What this means

  • Executable policy entries accept one supported name or path, rejecting shell expressions, arguments and invalid basename forms. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • Executable policy entries accept one supported name or path, rejecting shell expressions, arguments and invalid basename forms.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the entry against an executable name or supported exact path; remove flags, pipes and shell substitutions.

How to fix it

  • Replace the entry with a bare executable name (for example curl) or a path made only of letters, digits and _ . + @ - separated by slashes, with no arguments, whitespace, pipes or substitutions; the policy stores only the basename. See executable_basename in src/agent_runtime/capability_policy.py and resubmit through POST /api/agent/capabilities/validate.
  • Enter an executable name such as curl or an exact executable path; remove command arguments and shell expressions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended executable preference normalizes to a valid program basename.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
